item.title: Mounting an Everpure Cloud Azure Native Snapshot for Recovery on Linux
item.description: Are you looking for a way to get a few files back from an Everpure Cloud Azure Native snapshot without overwriting the live volume? The portal gives you two options today: overwrite the volume group, or restore the snapshot into a brand new volume group. Overwrite is destructive, and a new volume group means a new iSCSI target to mount on the VM. What I usually want is the old copy of one volume mounted next to the current one, so I can copy back what I need and throw the copy away. So I wrote a script that does exactly that. I started with Linux, and in Part 2 I do the same thing on Windows.

item.title: Mounting an Everpure Cloud Azure Native Snapshot for Recovery on Windows
item.description: Are you running Windows VMs on Everpure Cloud Azure Native and need a few files back from a snapshot without touching the live volume? In Part 1 I cloned one volume from the latest volume group snapshot and mounted it next to the original on Linux. This time it’s Windows. The Azure side is exactly the same, the guest side is where Windows does its own thing.
